value.body: Biotechnology (B.Tech / B.E.) applies engineering to living systems. You study cell and molecular biology, microbiology, biochemistry, genetic engineering, bioprocess engineering and bioinformatics, with a lot of lab work. It leads to work in biopharma, vaccines, diagnostics, and food and agri biotech, and often to higher study or research.

value.title: How you get in
value.body: You choose the branch at counselling, after the entrance exam. JEE Advanced rank is used for IITs; JEE Main rank for NITs, IIITs and other centrally funded institutes — all allotted through JoSAA. State colleges use state counselling with a state CET (EAMCET, MHT-CET, KCET, WBJEE and others) or, in Tamil Nadu (TNEA), Class 12 marks. Private universities may run their own tests. Class 12 with Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics is the usual requirement; some state and private colleges also admit students with Biology for this branch, so check each college's rules.

value.title: At a glance
items: Many first jobs are lab, production or quality roles; research-focused roles often expect an M.Tech, M.Sc or PhD.
Biopharma and vaccine plants work under GMP rules, so careful documentation is part of daily work.
Government research posts usually need a master's degree or PhD, or a research fellowship such as CSIR-NET JRF.
Some graduates move into bioinformatics, data or software roles.
